column3: NASB begins with “And he stood on the sand of the seashore,” which is 12:18 in the Greek numbering. It follows the critical text (“blasphemous names”); “rising” is rendered “coming up,” and “royal crowns” “diadems.”
NASB follows the critical text; it supplies “were … those of.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “I saw”; “marveled after” is rendered “was amazed and followed after.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the dragon, because he gave”).
NASB follows the critical text (“forty-two months”); “great things” is rendered “arrogant words.”
NASB follows the critical text (without “and” before “those”); NASB adds “that is.”
NASB follows the critical text (“and people”).
NASB follows the critical text (“whose name”); it joins “from the foundation of the world” to “written.”

The first line follows the critical text; NASB supplies “is destined for.” NASB’s “if anyone kills with the sword” matches the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “if anyone is to be killed with the sword.”
NASB follows the critical text (“to worship”); “on behalf of it” is rendered “in his presence.”
NASB follows the critical text; “has lived” is rendered “has come to life.”
NASB follows the critical text (“to be given a mark”); “servants” is rendered “slaves.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “or”; it supplies “he provides” and “either.”
NASB follows the critical text (“six hundred and sixty-six”); “count” is rendered “calculate.”
